**Observation Log:**

- [TEMPORAL] Session Date: 2023/05/26 (Fri) 07:54
- [FACT] The user works on mathematical or logical problems.
- [PREFERENCE] The user experiences difficulty finding solutions to problems during the day.
- [PREFERENCE] The user finds solutions while falling asleep and sometimes while waking up.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] The phenomenon of finding solutions while falling asleep is called the incubation period.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] The incubation period refers to the process of unconsciously working on a problem in the mind, even when not actively thinking about it.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] During the incubation period, the brain continues to process information and make connections, leading to breakthroughs.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] The process of "sleeping on it" is a normal part of problem-solving.
- [PREFERENCE] The user most often finds solutions before falling asleep.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] There may not be a significant difference between finding a solution before falling asleep or upon waking up, as both are part of the incubation period.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Letting the mind relax and wander can help make new connections and find solutions that may not have been thought of while actively working on the problem.
